post_title: Marketing Through Story and Understanding the Customer
meta_description: Mike Moll joins The Story Engine with Kyle Gray to talk about messaging that connects because it speaks to what the customer already feels.
tldr: Good messaging starts with understanding the customer, not with clever words.
People buy when they feel understood, so your story should mirror their problem back to them.
A short personalized video is one of the simplest ways to build trust early.
intro_html:
The Story Engine, hosted by Kyle Gray, is about using story to make marketing easier and more powerful. That is a topic I care about, because most marketing fails on message long before it fails on tactics.

We talked about how the strongest story is not the flashiest one. It is the one that shows your customer you understand where they are stuck.

sections.html:
People try to fix weak marketing with better words. Usually the problem is deeper. They do not understand the customer well enough to speak to them. Once you know the exact problem someone is losing sleep over, the words get simple.

People buy when they feel understood, not when they understand you. So the job of your story is to mirror the customer's problem back to them so clearly that they think you have been reading their mind.

This works one to one as well as it works at scale. A short personalized video, forty seconds to a bit over a minute, lets you show a specific person that you get their situation. That builds trust early, before any pitch.

Being useful and clear in public is also how authority gets built over time. I got into that on The Thoughtful Entrepreneur and the Sage Thought Leadership Podcast.

about_blurb_html: The Story Engine, hosted by business storytelling expert Kyle Gray, helps founders and marketers use story, content, and copywriting to make marketing easier. Episodes focus on turning a personal story and hard-won expertise into a message that connects.
